findings.reason: the plan would build a parallel test file and a duplicated resolution step where the owner and its parity tests already exist. Named owner: `resolve_project_repository` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:250) and the `dispatch()` prologue (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:6605). Note also that the plan's write paths omit `reckon/cli.py`, yet that is where the dry-run branch diverges from the launch branch (reckon/cli.py:2062-2087), so the change likely cannot land inside `dispatch.py` alone.
findings.text: the plan proposes two new test files, `tests/test_dry_run_resolves_the_real_call.py` and `tests/test_member_resolution_is_single_valued.py` (§2, §3 write paths), while the identical machinery and a precedent for exactly this defect already exist and should be extended: `tests/test_dry_run_reaches_admission.py` documents the same defect one gate over ("the command's dry-run branch called plan_dispatch with no session and no watch_required, the gate was never evaluated"), `tests/test_dry_run_predicts_the_launcher.py:1` already asserts dry-run/launcher parity end to end, and `tests/test_crew_dryrun.py`, `tests/test_dry_run_shows_each_set_override.py`, `tests/test_every_dry_run_refusal_carries_the_echo.py`, `tests/test_plan_review_dispatch.py` and `tests/test_plan_review_gate.py` all cover this surface. §2's claim that the resolution "calls already exist on the real path and are simply not reached when dry_run is set" is also wrong: both paths reach `plan_dispatch` (`reckon/cli.py:2064` for dry-run, `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:6666` for the real call), and the divergence is only that the real caller resolves `repo_root` and `authority` first (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:6605`, `6619`) and passes them in (`repo=repo_root`, `authority=authority`), while the dry-run caller passes the raw `--repo`. An implementer acting on the plan's wording would add new resolution inside the dry-run branch or inside `plan_dispatch` instead of routing both callers through the existing owner.

findings.reason: the plan must name the owner to extend (unify `plan_dispatch`'s member block with `dispatch()`'s roster lookup, or move both behind one call) and fix the root-cause attribution, or the fix will not be single-valued.
findings.text: §3 asks to make member resolution single-valued but never names that member resolution has two independent sites: inside `plan_dispatch` at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5317 (gated by `member and (local or backend_override is not None or default_backend_override is not None)`, reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5304-5306) and again inside `dispatch()` at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:7049 (gated by `named_member`). Because the `plan_dispatch` site is gated on the backend flags, a plain `--member X` dispatch never resolves the member there at all — which is the `--repo`-naming divergence §1 measures — so §3's stated decision ("is a member resolvable from the project alone, or does it require a repository?") is aimed at the wrong discriminator. Deciding the repository question without unifying the two sites leaves a third member able to acquire a third behaviour, which §3's own done-when forbids.

findings.reason: without naming the owning mechanism the plan will fork repository resolution a fourth time and drift from the mount semantics the real call relies on.
findings.text: §2 proposes "moving the line the dry run stops at" so the dry run performs the repository resolution the real call performs, but `plan_dispatch` already resolves the repository at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5242-5243 and again at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5312-5313, and `dispatch()` resolves it a third time at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:6605 — three sites for one decision, owned by `resolve_project_repository` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:250). The plan names none of them and does not say whether the fix extends `resolve_project_repository`/the `dispatch()` prologue (the honest change, since the divergence is the caller, not the function) or adds a fourth conditional inside `plan_dispatch`.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds no module; behaviour stays inside `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` behind the existing `plan_dispatch` interface, which already hides routing, authority, validation and admission behind one `as_dict()` result.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 asks for single-valued member resolution without naming that member resolution has two sites in `dispatch.py`, and §2's "move the stopping line" would duplicate the repo/authority resolution that the `dispatch()` prologue already owns rather than extending it.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; the plan adds no CLI option, no MCP view, no public definition and no refusal family (the refusals it surfaces, `plan-unavailable` and `plan-review-missing`, already exist and are only reached earlier than they are today), so there is no added surface for the sections to retire or merge.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan adds no new machinery, but it mis-describes the existing one: it claims the real call's resolution "calls already exist on the real path and are simply not reached when dry_run is set" (§2), while in fact both paths call the same `plan_dispatch`, and the divergence is that `dispatch()` pre-resolves the repository and authority before the call, and the CLI dry-run branch does not; it also ignores an existing family of dry-run parity tests it should extend.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan adds no wrapper over existing machinery; it removes a false-`ok`, it does not forward to an existing reader.
